headline: Judge approves $7.25bn Roundup cancer settlement
pages: A Missouri judge on Friday approved a $7.25 billion settlement of lawsuits claiming Bayer's Roundup weedkiller causes cancer. Judge Timothy Boyer called it fair, reasonable and adequate. The nationwide deal covers Roundup users who already have non-Hodgkin lymphoma and those who develop it in the future. Payments range from $10,000 to $165,000 depending on how often someone used the product, when they were diagnosed and how severe the illness is. Bayer will pay into a fund annually for up to 21 years. Some attorneys objected that the money was not enough, but the judge said he did not want to delay payments to sick people.

Bayer has already paid roughly $10 billion to resolve Roundup cases and denies the product causes cancer. In June, the Supreme Court ruled 7-2 for Bayer in a separate case. Why it matters: the deal limits a major legal liability for the company. Source: BBC.
